chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub: A man in Hamadhan mentioned that his father had passed away, and he was unaware of this matter, so he made a will at the time of death, instructing that something be given in the way of Allah. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about it, how it should be done, and we informed him that the deceased was unaware of this matter but had made a will at the time of death.
He said: 'If a man had made a will to me to place his wealth with a Jew or a Christian, I would place it with them. Indeed, Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, says:
So whoever changes it after he has heard it, the sin is only upon those who change it. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
Look for someone who is engaged in these paths (meaning the frontier defense posts), and send it to him.
ai.seo_question: How should a will be executed if the deceased gave specific instructions but was not well-versed in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq to illustrate the principle of fidelity to the testator's intent (wasiyya), even if the deceased lacked specific religious knowledge or designated a non-Muslim. By citing Quran 2:181, the Imam emphasizes that the sin rests solely on those who alter the bequest, thereby validating the transfer to the 'thughur' (frontier fighters) as a valid charitable expenditure. This highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in applying general Quranic principles to specific fiscal bequests.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5463 - Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaʿqub:
A man in Hamadhan mentioned that his father had passed away. His father was unaware of this matter (the teachings of the Ahl Al-Bayt), and before his death, he made a will instructing that something be given in the way of Allah (swt).
Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about how to fulfill this will, and it was explained to Imam (as) that the deceased was unaware of the truth but had made a will at the time of his death.
Abu Abdullah (as) said: "If a man had made a will to me to distribute his wealth to a Jew or a Christian, I would fulfill it for them. Indeed, Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says:
'But whoever changes it after hearing it, the sin is only upon those who change it. Verily, Allah (swt) is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.'" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:181)
Then Imam (as) added: "Look for someone who is engaged in these paths (meaning the frontier defense posts), and send it to him."
